- When sentiment is positive (≥0.3) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent peak) should be capped at +5% of recent range to prevent overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, adjust downward by 2–3% per week until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 3–5% below forecast, reduce forecast baseline by 2–3% for next period.  
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., >0.5) should trigger a 1–2% downward adjustment in forecast to account for volatility overreaction.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.1–0.2) and forecast is erratic, favor smoother trend continuation over sharp reversals.
